html:
SMTO-SKL-0046 — The Drive upload stopped making progress

GUID: 1b480b27-4838-585c-b3b7-54ebc9dd2e8e
Slug: google-drive-upload-failed
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • SMTO kept sending the next part of your file, but Google stopped accepting it, so SMTO gave up. The upload most likely didn't finish, but check Drive before trying again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether your action already happened: open the destination folder in Google Drive and look for the file by name and size. If Google did finish the upload, sending it again would create a duplicate.
  2. Make sure the computer running SMTO has a steady internet connection, for example by opening a few websites on it. A shaky connection is a common reason uploads stop moving forward.
  3. If the file isn't in Drive, ask SMTO to upload it again and approve the request. Once you know nothing was saved, a fresh upload is safe.

What success looks like

  • Exactly one copy of the file is in the Drive folder, at the expected size.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, with the file's size. Don't keep restarting the upload without checking Drive in between.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The resumable Drive upload stalled: Google acknowledged the same byte offset more than twice in a row, so SMTO stopped sending chunks (upload_failed).

What this means

  • A resumable upload reports the same acknowledged offset more than twice. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • A resumable upload reports the same acknowledged offset more than twice.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect last acknowledged offset and exact destination/correlation.

How to fix it

  • uploads.upload raises upload_failed when the session's confirmed Range offset fails to advance on three consecutive chunk attempts. Confirm no completed upload exists (for upload, a file with the operation's smto_operation appProperty; for replace_contents, the target file's size and md5Checksum), check the Server host's network path to googleapis.com, then start one new upload.
  • Inspect the exact Drive state and retry only after confirming no completed upload exists.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact Drive state and retry only after confirming no completed upload exists.

How to verify the fix

  • Provider state is reconciled before resuming supported remaining bytes or starting new work.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
